name: Transco Sundance Expansion
researcher_notes: Not on the roster: P0271 is the Transco main line system row and no row covers Sundance. Qualifies as a new expansion row under the Transcontinental Gas Pipeline name. The EIA August 2026 release, sheet Historical Projects (1996-2024), Excel row 232, lists it as completed May 2002, 38 miles, 42 and 48 inch, 230 MMcf/d added, cost 134.67 million dollars, FERC docket CP00-165. Independent sources agree. A Federal Register notice of application from April 2000 lists four loops: DeSoto 12.03 mi of 42 inch in Clarke County, Mississippi to Choctaw County, Alabama; Summerville 9.36 mi of 48 inch in Alabama; Kings Mountain 8.97 mi of 42 inch in North Carolina; Mooresville 7.67 mi of 42 inch in North Carolina. These sum to 38.03 miles. It also asks for 236,383 dekatherms per day of new capacity and a May 2002 start. A July 2000 Federal Register notice of environmental review says about 38 miles of 42 and 48 inch pipe. The 2001 annual report of Transco says about 228 MMcf/d from Station 65 in Louisiana to Georgia, South Carolina and North Carolina, 38 miles of loop, and a cost near 134 million dollars, with the FERC order dated March 29, 2001. Start and end states are the first and last loop locations (Mississippi and North Carolina). The EIA lists Louisiana to Virginia because the capacity runs from Station 65 in Louisiana, but no new pipe was found there. Capacity is the EIA figure, 230 MMcf/d. The annual report says 228. The EIA project dates the in-service month as May 2002. Route not researched: no official map found, so route columns are left blank for a person to map from the FERC filing mileposts (MP 772.81-784.84, 851.46-860.82, 1247.03-1256.00, 1287.11-1294.78). The EIA lists Georgia among its states, but the loops found are in Mississippi, Alabama and North Carolina; Georgia work was compression. Owner matched the existing entity Transco in the gazetteer. The projects used compression at Stations 115 and 125 as well.
